name: MindBridge NovaMesh Entry Neural Interface
description:
The MindBridge NovaMesh Entry is the most widely installed first BCI in GLMZ's history — a stripped-down, cost-optimized neural interface designed to bring basic feed access, civic identity integration, and payment functionality to the widest possible demographic at the lowest possible price point. The NovaMesh uses a three-point subdural mesh — the minimum viable contact array for stable feed connectivity — paired with MindBridge's NovaBridge firmware, which prioritizes stability and civic compliance over performance. Bandwidth is limited to 1.8 Gbps, sufficient for text messaging, AR navigation overlays, payment authorization, and civic ID verification, but inadequate for demanding multi-stream professional applications or high-resolution entertainment feeds. The installation procedure takes 20 minutes and can be performed at any of MindBridge's 400-plus certified kiosks across GLMZ, including locations in lower Tier 2 districts and select Tier 1 access points.

The NovaMesh Entry is the BCI that plugs people into the city — literally. GLMZ's civic infrastructure increasingly assumes neural connectivity for basic services: transit payment, benefit disbursement, civic alert systems, employment verification, and building access all route through neural-mesh handshakes that the unconnected cannot access. The NovaMesh is often the first step into this system for Tier 1 residents receiving civic integration subsidies, for new arrivals registering for city services, and for adolescents receiving their government-subsidized first installation at age 14. It carries the social weight of its price point — to wear a NovaMesh in Tier 3 is to advertise that you haven't upgraded yet — but in the communities it actually serves, it is a genuine lifeline rather than a compromise.
installation_requirements: MindBridge certified kiosk; no anesthetic required for most recipients; 20-minute procedure; government-subsidized installation available for qualifying Tier 1-2 residents
rejection_risk: Minimal — three-point mesh is the simplest contact configuration available; 99.1% acceptance rate; designed to the broadest possible biocompatibility standard including common genetic variants and prior medical history flags
maintenance: Automatic firmware updates via passive sync; kiosk-based diagnostic check recommended annually; no manual recalibration required in standard operation; MindBridge civic-tier support line available 24 hours
specifications: {"bandwidth": "1.8 Gbps neural throughput", "channels": "3 subdural mesh points", "encryption": "AES-128 civic standard", "battery": "inductive charging, 24-hour active cycle", "latency": "18ms average feed response", "storage": "512GB onboard cache", "connectivity": "MeshNet, civic ID, payment rail, transit integration, emergency broadcast, civic alert system", "limitations": "single active process; no multi-stream; no professional terminal handshake; no smart-link compatibility"}
side_effects: Feed-stutter under load — attempting to run more than one active application simultaneously causes perceptible lag and occasional dropout, a constant frustration for users pushing the hardware's limits
Civic-alert bleed — the NovaMesh's emergency broadcast channel cannot be muted or filtered, meaning users in high-alert zones experience mandatory interruptions that cannot be dismissed

Low-level background connectivity anxiety in users who previously lived without neural mesh — the always-on status of the civic ID and payment channels creates a persistent low-grade awareness of being monitored that takes months to normalize
Thermal sensitivity near installation points during high-bandwidth periods; a faint warmth behind the ear that users colloquially call 'the hum'
cultural_context: The NovaMesh is the BCI of civic minimum — the floor of connectivity in a city where being unconnected is increasingly equivalent to being invisible to its systems. MindBridge markets it with language about 'connection for everyone' and 'the first step,' and there is genuine social good in what it does: it plugs people into the infrastructure of urban survival. But it also cements MindBridge's position as the data broker of the city's most economically vulnerable population, collecting behavioral and location data from the largest single-BCI installation base in GLMZ. Civic advocacy groups have spent years attempting to legislate data protections for NovaMesh users with limited success. In Tier 3 and above, a NovaMesh is a visible marker of economic precarity; in Tier 1 and lower Tier 2, it is simply what you have.
known_users: Tier 1 residents receiving civic integration subsidies
Recent arrivals registering for GLMZ civic services
Elderly residents whose prior hardware has been downgraded through poverty
Gig-economy workers in the lowest-margin logistics and service sectors
story_hooks: GLMZ's civic services have quietly made the NovaMesh's civic ID channel a prerequisite for benefit disbursement, effectively forcing Tier 1 residents to accept neural installation to access food assistance and housing credits. A community organizer is building a legal challenge — and has received a credible threat telling them to stop.

A dormant subroutine in NovaMesh firmware predating version 3.2 — installed in units across Tier 1 and lower Tier 2 — has been remotely activated by an unknown actor. It is not doing anything visible yet. It is simply listening. The players need to find out what it is waiting to hear.

A MindBridge kiosk technician in a Tier 2 district has been quietly altering NovaMesh installations for six months — adding an unlicensed fourth contact point that dramatically improves bandwidth but also creates a passive neural-read channel accessible to someone with the right equipment. The technician claims they were trying to help their community. The question is who gave them the modified firmware.
